extracted.intended_audience: Patent practitioners (registered patent attorneys/agents), respondents in USPTO disciplinary matters, and counsel advising practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements used by the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline to evaluate alleged professional misconduct by patent practitioners, the related MPEP/Code obligations, and the remedial sanctions and compliance obligations imposed by Final Orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and applicability of USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent ... has been an agent registered to practice patent law before the Office (Registration Number ... ) and is subject to the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being a registered agent/attorney brings one under the USPTO disciplinary rules (37 C.F.R. Part 10); registered practitioners are accountable for those standards in disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate entities not entitled to represent before the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: PPi, as a corporate entity, was not and could not be registered to practice before the Office within the meaning of 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.5-11.11; therefore, it was not lawfully entitled to represent persons having prospective or immediate business before the Office in the preparation and prosecution of patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only individuals registered under USPTO rules (or other specifically authorized entities) may practice before the Office; contracting corporate entities that are not registered may not lawfully represent clients before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPEP format compliance for filed applications (MPEP § 709.01(m))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office rejected claims in the '970 application ... in part because Respondent did not comply with the format requirements set forth in § 709.01(m) of the Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent applications must meet MPEP format requirements (e.g., §709.01(m)); failure to comply can lead to office action rejections and adverse disciplinary findings. Use proofing and checklist procedures to ensure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPEP drafting compliance (MPEP § 608.01(n) and related drafting standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part of the '970 B application also was not drafted in compliance with MPEP § 608.01(n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive drafting requirements of the MPEP must be followed when preparing applications; drafting errors that violate MPEP provisions may be cited in office actions and disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to provide complete and accurate information to clients in a timely manner (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) and § 10.23(c)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4), as further defined by 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(2)(i), by not providing complete and accurate information in a timely manner to a client about the status of a pending application pending before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must promptly and accurately inform clients of the status of pending proceedings (e.g., receipt of office actions, deadlines, extension petitions). Failure to notify clients or to disclose extension requests constitutes a violation of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper handling of client advanced fees and trust account requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: From March 2000 until September 2006, PPi deposited advanced fees received from clients into its general operating account, which was not a client trust account. Respondent caused PPi to establish and use an Attorney IOLTA Trust Account in accordance with the requirements of the State Bar of Wisconsin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advanced fees for patent prosecution should be handled per applicable state bar rules (e.g., deposited into a client trust/IOLTA account as required). Misapplication of client funds or failure to maintain required trust accounts can lead to discipline and remedial requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business arrangement and entity-related professional responsibility rules (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.48, 10.49, 10.78, 10.112(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent violated 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.48, 10.49, 10.78, and 10.112(b) based on the business arrangement with PPi as they pertain to PPi's preparation and prosecution of patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must ensure that business structures, fee arrangements, and the provision of legal services comply with USPTO regulations and the Code of Professional Responsibility; improper business arrangements with non-registrant entities or failure to disclose/structure matters correctly implicate these rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely response to Office actions and procedural deadlines (including extension petitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office issued a non-final office action rejecting claims ... informing Respondent that a response thereto was due in three months. Respondent filed a petition for an extension in time to respond to the office action but did not promptly notify the client of the office action nor of the extension petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must monitor deadlines, file timely responses or proper extension petitions, and notify clients about office actions and extensions. Failure to act timely or to communicate with clients about deadlines can harm clients and trigger discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications with third-party intermediaries and responsibility to keep the inventor/client informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent deferred to communications via the inventor's father as an intermediary and acknowledges difficulties communicating with the inventor; he failed to timely notify the client of the office action and extension filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when intermediaries are used, the practitioner remains responsible for ensuring the client/inventor is informed about critical developments and deadlines. Reliance on intermediaries does not excuse failure to communicate with the actual client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to document substantive agreements with examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director asserts the USPTO examiner could not recall any conversation with Respondent and explained that he would have documented the file had any substantive agreement been reached. Respondent agrees no substantive agreement was reached and that the conversation was general in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a practitioner reaches any substantive agreement or understanding with an examiner that affects prosecution, it should be evidenced in the record/file; oral, undocumented promises or purported agreements are unreliable and may be disregarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreement procedural requirement (37 C.F.R. § 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed settlement agreement ... satisfies the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 and resolves all disciplinary action by the United States Patent and Trademark Office arising from the allegations investigated by OED and the evidence submitted to the USPTO's Committee on Discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements to resolve disciplinary matters before the USPTO must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 to be accepted and to resolve the Office's disciplinary claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reprimand, publication, and notice to state bar as disciplinary sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent be ... publicly reprimanded; The OED Director shall publish this Final Order; The OED Director shall publish the following Notice in the Official Gazette; The OED Director shall give notice to the Wisconsin State Bar that Respondent has been reprimanded and placed on probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary outcomes can include public reprimand, mandatory publication of the discipline (e.g., Official Gazette), and notice to state licensing authorities; practitioners should expect public and cross-jurisdictional consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory continuing legal education (CLE) in ethics and proof requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall within twelve months ... enroll, complete, and receive Continuing Legal Education credit ... for at least one course where the subject matter includes ethics and professional responsibility in the context of client communications; within thirteen months the OED Director must have received corroborating proof including documentary evidence of course attendance, a description of course content, and copy of all written materials provided to participants or other corroborating proof acceptable to the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When CLE is imposed as a remedial sanction, practitioners must provide detailed corroborating proof of course completion and content; merely attending a course is insufficient without documentary proof acceptable to the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to review and correct prior filings for MPEP compliance and report corrective actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall: 1) within three months ... review all pending patent applications that he has filed with the Office to determine if they have been drafted in accordance with sections 608.01(m) and (n) of the MPEP and, if not so drafted, file appropriate papers with the Office in each patent application to correct any such drafting errors; 2) within four months ... file with the OED Director an affidavit identifying all pending patent applications reviewed, identifying the applications amended, and stating the corrective action taken in each application; and 3) otherwise require Respondent bear all the costs and expenses of the provisions of this subparagraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrective remediation may be required: practitioners may be ordered to review past work, correct MPEP violations in pending files, file affidavits describing actions taken, and bear costs for the corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetary restitution to clients and affidavit proof of compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall: 1) within thirty days ... deliver to G. the monetary compensation reflected ... and 2) within forty-five days ... the OED Director must receive from Respondent an affidavit demonstrating that Respondent timely complied with the provisions of this subparagraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary orders can mandate refunds or partial refunds to clients; compliance must be documented by affidavit and timely submitted to the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probationary period and consequences for noncompliance (Order to Show Cause; suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a twenty-four (24) month probationary period ... In the event that the OED Director is of the opinion that during the twenty-four month probationary period Respondent failed to comply with any of the terms of this Final Order, the OED Director shall issue to Respondent an Order to Show Cause ... grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond ... if continued noncompliance the OED Director shall deliver to the USPTO Director ... for imposition of a six-month suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation with specific compliance tasks may be imposed; failure to comply can trigger an Order to Show Cause, short response windows, and referral for immediate suspension. Practitioners should strictly comply with probationary terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate effect of suspension and reinstatement procedures (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58–11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent is suspended pursuant to the terms of this Final Order, Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; If Respondent is suspended ... the OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; after completing the entire suspension ... Respondent may apply for reinstatement ... upon filing a petition for reinstatement that complies fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60; any such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the immediate suspension of Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension is effective immediately upon imposition; reinstatement requires satisfying the specific regulatory petition and procedures under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58–11.60; seeking review does not stay suspension unless otherwise ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of disciplinary proceeding considered in future matters (aggravating/rebuttal use)
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of this disciplinary proceeding, including this Final Order, shall be considered 1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct ... and/or 2) in any future disciplinary proceeding a) as an aggravating factor to be taken into consideration in determining any discipline to be imposed and/or b) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary records are persistent and may be used against a practitioner in subsequent matters as aggravation or to rebut claims; practitioners should be aware of long-term consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties bear their own costs unless otherwise ordered
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement orders may specify cost allocation; absent specific order, parties often bear their own costs, but other remedial costs (e.g., corrections, refunds) may be separately ordered and borne by respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial best practices: use of checklists and additional training
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent has created and currently uses a two-page checklist of USPTO requirements when drafting and reviewing patent applications as one means of ensuring compliance with MPEP requirements; he attended relevant CLE and a Practicing Law Institute seminar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of remediation or best practice, practitioners should adopt drafting/review checklists, obtain targeted training in claim drafting/prosecution, and proactively correct errors to reduce risk of future discipline.
